name: Iron Oxide Yellow (CI 77492)
regulatory: FDA 21 CFR 73.2250 (color additive); EU Cosmetic Reg. Annex IV. Same regulatory status as red and black iron oxides; not a UV filter under FDA monograph.
metric: E(1%, 1cm) -- effective mass attenuation (absorption + Mie scattering) for pigment-grade ~300 nm primary particles in cosmetic film. E1% = 10 x k(L/g/cm).
primary_sources: Sherman & Waite 1985 Am Mineral 70:1262 -- goethite Fe3+ d-d bands at 480, 660, 920 nm; CT below 460 nm. Goethite is ~1 stop more transparent in green/red than hematite.
Morris et al. 1985 J Geophys Res 90:3126 -- submicron goethite powder reflectance: minimum ~430 nm, sharp rise to >70% reflectance at 600 nm (yellow color).
Wells & Buckley 2003 / Cudahy 2000 Reflectance Spectra of Iron Oxides -- canonical goethite reflectance spectrum (used in mineralogy/remote sensing).
Sileo et al. 2007 Geochim Cosmochim Acta -- goethite 2.55 eV optical bandgap, reflectance edge at 496 nm.
Dumbuya et al. 2020 J Drugs Dermatol 19:712 -- VLPF data for iron-oxide blends including yellow component.
Lyons et al. 2021 J Am Acad Dermatol 84:1393 -- review of visible-light protection in tinted sunscreens; notes 'yellow iron oxide attenuates below ~500 nm' (the HEV band).
physical_notes: Goethite is acicular (needle-shape) ~50-200 nm long pigment crystallites that aggregate into 200-500 nm bundles in cosmetic dispersion. The acicular habit gives stronger forward-scattering than equant hematite.

Bandgap 2.5 eV (496 nm) is a sharp edge -- goethite is a strong absorber for HEV (400-500 nm) but rapidly transparent above 500 nm. This makes it the IDEAL pigment for blue-light blockade specifically (lambda < 500 nm).
Fe3+ d-d shoulder at ~480 nm overlaps the bandgap edge, broadening the effective absorption into 460-510 nm. CT band below 400 nm extends UV protection.

Above 550 nm goethite is highly transparent -- the yellow color comes from selective absorption of blue/violet only. This is why yellow iron oxide is a poor HEV BROADBAND blocker but excellent blue-violet absorber.

concentration_nonlinearity.model: f(c) = 1 - alpha * tanh(max(0, c - c0) / scale)
concentration_nonlinearity.rationale: Same family as red. Goethite saturates slightly slower than hematite because its acicular habit resists dense packing -- effective scale is a bit larger.
concentration_nonlinearity.source: Same anchor set as red; goethite-specific acicular packing gives slower saturation (Hupel 2024 density argument is weaker since goethite films are less dense).

particle_size_correction.model: multiplier on E1%(lambda); pigment-grade is the cosmetic norm
particle_size_correction.source: Mie theory for goethite n~2.4+0.3i in visible; size optimum ~250-350 nm primary for HEV. Acicular grade may show 10-15% higher effective mass attenuation per the long-axis aspect ratio.

hev_model.absorbance: A(lambda) = E1%(lambda) x f(c) x g(d) x 100 x c_active_g_per_cm2

validation.source: Inferred from Ezekwe 2024 blend deconvolution; yellow contributes ~30-40% of HEV in typical 3-pigment tint
Lyons 2021 review -- 'yellow attenuates below 500 nm' anchor

validation.formulation: Tinted facial sunscreen with 1% Yellow + 0.5% Red + 0.3% Black (typical foundation tint, 1.3 mg/cm2)
validation.source: Mahmoud 2010 equivalent tint composition; this row is illustrative of multi-pigment additivity

validation_summary.note: Yellow iron oxide HEV contribution is the smallest of the three; validation uses blend-deconvolution since pure mono-pigment data is rare.

caveats: Peak E1% = 60 is for pigment-grade goethite ~300 nm primary, ~1.3 mg/cm2 film, <2% loading. Old chart value 1800 was overstated by ~30x.
Goethite is the WEAKEST of the three iron oxides at 400-500 nm but still a useful HEV blocker because its absorption is concentrated in the most-damaging blue-violet band.
Above 550 nm goethite is essentially transparent -- a 5% goethite film at 1.3 mg/cm2 transmits >95% of green/red light. This is desirable for cosmetic blendability across skin tones.
f(c) saturates more slowly than hematite (scale 4 vs 3) because acicular particles pack less densely; less film-density penalty at high loading.
Goethite dehydrates to hematite at >200 deg C -- not a concern for cosmetic processing, noted for completeness.
Real tinted sunscreens use Yellow:Red:Black mass ratios near 6:3:1 (foundation-style) or 4:2:1 to match Fitzpatrick III-IV skin tone; HEV blockade is the SUM of contributions plus TiO2/ZnO.
